newsitem.title: GERMANY: WESTLB SEES MORE MARK WEAKENING, NO BUBA HIKE SOON.
newsitem.headline: WESTLB SEES MORE MARK WEAKENING, NO BUBA HIKE SOON.

text.p: The dollar has room to continue climbing against the mark, and the Bundesbank is unlikely to raise interest rates in the near future, Westdeutsche Landesbank (WestLB) said on Thursday.

But expectations of a rate increase will persist because August import prices are expected to rise four percent and consumer price inflation (CPI) should hit two percent in the autumn, WestLb said. Two-percent CPI is seen as a criticical level for the Bundesbank, so bond yields should fall, it said in its interim report.

"WestLB's economists interpret the rapid rise of the U.S. dollar as a reappraisal by the markets of the two 'large corporations' U.S. and the Federal Republic of Germany," West LB said. "This reappraisal is clearly in favour of the U.S.

"As this situation is unlikely to change fundamentally in the foreseeable future and in view of the fact that a large monetary union with heterogeneous participants is looming ever larger, there is scope for the dollar to climb further still."
Against that background, interest rates in the money and bond markets had now bottomed out.

WestLB said it did not expect the Bundesbank to raise its interest rates in the near-term to help the mark, but market expectations of a cut are likely to push up long-term bond yields by half a percentage point by year-end.
The dollar has risen about 20 percent against the mark but gave back six pfennigs over the past week. It was quoted at 1.8335 marks at 1050 GMT.
The yield on the benchmark 6.0 percent 10-year German bond was 5.67 percent.
